properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared dependency in the wallet frontend's yarn.lock (transitive, via the zksync/web3 SDK stack — elliptic and friends). hash.js ships SHA-1/SHA-2 family implementations, so they are in the shipped bundle. No direct hash.js call site in first-party src/ — the app delegates all crypto to the SDKs; presence is what this entry records.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js is in the frontend dependency tree (@types/crypto-js is even a declared devDependency, so the app expects the library), and crypto-js ships MD5 among its modules. No first-party MD5 call site found in src/ — the algorithm ships with the library regardless.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same crypto-js@3.3.0 dependency as the MD5 entry: SHA-1 implementations ship in the frontend bundle. No first-party call site found in src/.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@1.3.1 is in the functions backend lockfile (transitive dependency of the deployed Firebase functions bundle); it ships RSA keygen/encrypt/sign plus X.509 handling. No first-party call site in functions/src (the backend's only direct crypto is createHmac in moonpay.sign.ts) — this records that RSA ships in the deployed bundle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All 9 sites are lockfile entries: 8 are ecdsa-sig-formatter@1.0.11 in functions/package-lock.json — the ECDSA (ES256) signature formatter used by jsonwebtoken, which is a direct dependency of firebase-admin v10, i.e. the backend's JWT verification stack; 1 site is the ECDSA-family dependency in yarn.lock (frontend web3 stack, e.g. elliptic via the zksync SDK). ECDSA ships in both bundles; no first-party ECDSA call site in functions/src or src/.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5 is in the frontend dependency tree — it is the crypto core of the zksync SDK (zkSync signing keys and crypto_box). X25519 key agreement (nacl.box) ships with it. No first-party call site in src/; the primitives execute inside the SDK (node_modules not present in this tree). Quantum-unsafe key agreement, harvestable if used for session/key exchange.

components.name: Node.js tls sessions on default settings (Node.js 16)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@3.0.1 is in yarn.lock — the password-based KDF behind Web3 Secret Storage keystores (ethers.js uses it for keystore import/export in the zksync SDK stack), i.e. wallet-file encryption. The scrypt parameters (N/r/p) are chosen inside the SDK and are not visible in this tree; presence is recorded here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same tweetnacl@0.14.5 dependency as the X25519 entry: nacl.secretbox (XSalsa20-Poly1305) ships in the frontend bundle. Symmetric AE — not Shor-vulnerable, rated well; recorded as dependency presence. No first-party call site in src/.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@1.3.1 in the functions backend lockfile ships X.509 certificate parsing/creation alongside RSA. No first-party cert-handling call site in functions/src; the deployed backend bundle carries the capability. Changeable here by adjusting the dependency tree (it arrives transitively via firebase-admin).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: jsonwebtoken@8.5.1 is a direct dependency of firebase-admin v10 (the backend's only auth library) — Firebase Auth mints and verifies RS256/HS256 JWTs with it. The first-party functions code never calls jwt.sign/verify directly; all JWT operations are delegated to firebase-admin. Presence of the quantum-vulnerable RSA-backed JWT signing stack in the deployed backend is what this records.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: jose@2.0.5 in the functions backend lockfile (transitive) ships JWS/JWE/JWK capabilities in the deployed bundle. No first-party call site found in functions/src.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: jws@3.2.2 in the functions backend lockfile — the JWS serialize/verify layer used by jsonwebtoken, which firebase-admin v10 uses for Firebase Auth tokens. Part of the backend's JWT stack (RS256 = RSA signatures under the hood); no first-party call site in functions/src.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: jwa@1.4.1 in the functions backend lockfile — implements the JWA algorithms (HS256, RS256, ES256...) that jws/jsonwebtoken use. Same firebase-admin JWT stack; no first-party call site in functions/src.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js@3.3.0 is declared in the frontend yarn.lock and @types/crypto-js is a first-party devDependency — the app's TS code expects the library even though no direct call site remains in src/. It ships MD5/SHA-1/SHA-2/AES/PBKDF2/HMAC implementations in the browser bundle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: jwa@1.4.1 declared in the functions backend lockfile — the JWA algorithm layer of the jsonwebtoken/firebase-admin JWT stack. Same logical asset chain as ALG-a57f6d5a (the JWA algorithm object), reached by its package name.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: jws@3.2.2 declared in the functions backend lockfile — the JWS serialization layer of the jsonwebtoken/firebase-admin JWT stack. Same logical asset chain as ALG-5bdcede9 (the JWS algorithm object), reached by its package name.
